title: Cartesian open diagrams and their compact-support comparison arrows
statement: Use normalized inverse-image squares and their d and chi arrows [def-pur-normalized-inverse-image-square] and constant-coefficient models [def-pur-constant-coefficient-topos-model]. An open model I is a left adjoint to the exact derived inverse image L, with invertible unit. An open square consists of an inverse-image square j:X→T, a subterminal sheaf U in T, equivalences Sh(X)≃Sh(T)/U and Sh(Xtilde)≃Sh(Ttilde)/(nu_T^{-1}U), identifications of both inverse-image functors with slice inverse image, and identification of nu_X with the induced slice inverse image. It includes open models in both coefficients on both systems. Its scalar comparison beta:S_T I_A≅I_B S_X is normalized by requiring the open-adjunction mate of beta^{-1} to be lambda_j^{-1}; its tilde comparison has the same normalization. Its site comparison e_R:N_T I_R≅Itilde_R N_X is normalized by requiring the open-adjunction mate of e_R^{-1} to be the inverse of the exact descended inverse-image square [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. A factorization consists of three vertices X,T,Y, this open square j and an inverse-image square p:T→Y, with both direct models on both systems. Define F_R=R_{p,R} I_{j,R}, Ftilde_R=R_{ptilde,R} I_{jtilde,R}, c=R_{p,B}(beta_j) chi_p, and C_R=R_{ptilde,R}(e_R) d_{p,R,I_j(-)}, inserting the functor associators; define ctilde by the same formula. These are specified natural transformations, without a mixed-square hypothesis.
